_comment: Which lines are `#כלול` inclusion directives — the corpus both readers run.
The rule exists twice: `engine/src/include.rs` splices the documents, and
`app/src/parts.ts` decides which ones to put on the compile request. They
decide different halves of one operation, so a line only one of them
recognises is a chapter the engine reports missing on a document that names
it correctly — and `parts.ts` had already written down, in prose, that
"the two implementations have to agree". This file is that sentence made
`name` is null when the line is not a directive at all.

cases.name: פרק (ג)
cases.why: a paren in the name — the scan must not stop at the first one
prose about the command is not the command: whole lines only
a space before the paren is not the call syntax on either side
an empty name names no document. Rust answered Some("") and the app filtered it, so the engine asked for a chapter called nothing and reported it missing
